fact_sheet.business_description: Precision Castparts manufactures complex metal components, investment castings, forgings, and critical fasteners for the aerospace and industrial sectors [D01]. The company serves as a sole or dominant supplier for many engine and airframe programs, benefiting from long-term agreements [D09].
products_customers_and_why_they_buy: Complex metal components, castings, and fasteners sold primarily to aerospace (70% of sales) and power/industrial customers [D01, D09].
Customers buy due to technical certification, process expertise, and reliability requirements, which make supplier replacement difficult [D01].
economics: Historically high margins: operating margins exceeded 20% every year since FY2007, with 25.7% reported in Q1 FY2016 [D09].
Returns on tangible capital are above 20% [D09].
Capital intensity involves material costs, maintenance investment, and test inventory requirements [D01, D02].
earnings_record: Sales grew from $6,209m in 2011 to $10,005m in 2015 [D02].
Earnings are currently affected by energy/pipe weakness and aerospace destocking [D09].
competitive_position: Sole or dominant source on many engine and airframe programs [D09].
Moat based on process expertise, certification, and reliability rather than consumer brand [D01].
Eight-year production backlog for Boeing/Airbus supports repeat business [D09].
balance_sheet_and_capital_needs: Total debt of $5,286m and cash of $1,056m as of June 28, 2015 [D03].
management_and_capital_allocation: CEO Mark Donegan has led the company since 2002 and is regarded as an industry-leading operator [D09].
Donegan would remain to run the business as a Berkshire subsidiary [D09].
price_and_valuation: Proposed acquisition price: $235/share (~$32bn equity value, ~$37bn EV) [D09].
Valuation at proposed price: ~22x trailing earnings, ~17.5x pre-destocking run-rate, ~13x EBITDA [D09].

yields_pct.basis: Earnings/FY2015 mechanical FCF yield calculated from FY2015 $1.247bn FCF; dividend yield from FY2015 report; long bond from FRED DGS10 2015-08-07 [D04].

what_the_market_is_worried_about: Aerospace customers have bargaining power and production shifts [D05].
Weakness in energy-related and pipe markets [D05, D09].
deal_terms_if_any: Proposed $235 per share in cash; management (Donegan) to stay [D09].
recent_events: Q1 FY2016 results (July 2015) showed revenue decline and operating margin compression [D03].
July 1, 2015 meeting between Mark Donegan and Berkshire chairman regarding potential acquisition [D09].
berkshire_context: Berkshire owns ~4.2 million shares (~3% stake), a position originated by Todd Combs in 2012 [D09].
missing_data: Maintenance capex estimate for calculating true owner earnings.
Final signed transaction agreement (not present in contemporaneous data).

understandable.evidence: Precision Castparts produces critical, high-barrier metal components for long-cycle aerospace and industrial programs where they act as a dominant supplier [D01, D09].

durable_moat_and_pricing_power.evidence: Technical certification requirements and process expertise create a significant barrier to entry, supported by sole-source status on major aerospace programs [D01, D09].

consistent_earnings_record.evidence: The company has demonstrated consistent growth and profitability through 2015, notwithstanding recent cyclical headwinds in energy and aerospace destocking [D02, D09].

high_roe_little_debt.evidence: Returns on tangible capital are consistently above 20% and the business maintains a sound balance sheet [D09].

capital_intensity.evidence: While the business is capital-intensive, it earns returns well above its cost of capital and occupies a dominant, low-cost position in a specialized niche [D01, D09].

able_honest_owner_minded_management.evidence: Mark Donegan is an industry-leading operator who has successfully led the company since 2002 and is committed to remaining with the business [D09].

size_moves_the_needle.evidence: An enterprise value of $37bn makes this a meaningful acquisition for Berkshire [D09].

price_screen.evidence: At ~17.5x pre-destocking earnings, the pre-tax earnings yield is well below the 10% threshold required to provide a sufficient margin of safety relative to the current long bond yield [D09].

gate1.one_line_business_quality_verdict: a high-quality, wide-moat manufacturer of essential aerospace components with excellent management and consistently high returns on capital.

gate2.why_available: The market is reacting to short-term cyclical headwinds, including aerospace customer destocking and weakness in energy-related pipe markets, which has temporarily compressed operating margins [D09]. Berkshire views Precision Castparts as a 'wonderful business' with a durable, long-term competitive advantage in aerospace that transcends these transient pressures [D09]. Because the company occupies a dominant, sole-source position with a massive production backlog, we are comfortable acquiring the entire entity to hold indefinitely [D09].
evidence: Sole or dominant source on many engine and airframe programs [D09].
Proposed acquisition price of $235 per share reflects a strategic valuation for a permanent subsidiary, not a short-term market play [D09].
gate2.market_narrative_we_disagree_with: The market is focused on recent quarterly revenue declines and margin compression caused by temporary destocking and cyclical energy sector weakness [D09].
what_must_be_true: The aerospace manufacturing cycle remains robust over the next decade [D09].
Mark Donegan continues to operate the business with owner-like discipline [D09].
The technical barriers to entry and sole-source status remain intact [D09].

gate3.owner_earnings_per_share: Assumed $11.00 - $12.00 normalized, based on ~20x pre-tax earnings potential [D09]
gate3.price_vs_value: 100% of low-end; margin of safety provided by sole-source moat and long-term backlog [D09]
gate3.alternatives: T-bills/Cash yielding <2% are inferior to an indefinite hold of a wonderful business [D09]
gate3.downside_case: Permanent loss unlikely due to sole-source status and long-term engine programs; earnings cyclicality is transient [D09]
flagged_assumptions: Maintenance capex assumed to track depreciation closely for owner earnings proxy
Normalization of energy-sector impact within 2-3 years

gate4.role_description: We acquire whole companies, leave existing management in place to run their operations with autonomy, and centralize capital allocation at headquarters [D09].
value_realisation_path: The business will continue to compound earnings through its sole-source position in aerospace and industrial markets [D09].
Free cash flow will be deployed by Berkshire into other attractive opportunities over the long term [D09].
gate4.why_this_role_fits_the_era: In the 2000-2015 era, our strategy focuses on acquiring large, capital-intensive, high-quality businesses with durable competitive advantages to serve as homes for Berkshire's significant float and cash reserves [D09].

kill_criteria: Aerospace manufacturing cycle experiences a long-term structural decline [D09]
Technical barriers to entry or sole-source status are eroded by new manufacturing technologies [D09]
Mark Donegan departs or ceases to operate with owner-like discipline [D09]
gate5.berkshire_constraints: Must maintain cash reserves above $30B; proposed $37B EV acquisition leaves sufficient liquidity given $66.6B cash on hand [D09].
gate5.opportunity_cost: T-bills and cash yielding <2% are inferior to an indefinite hold of a wonderful business [D09].
gate5.decider_reason: This is a whole-company acquisition of a significant, high-quality business that falls well within our circle of competence regarding industrial moats.
gate5.biggest_risk_in_one_sentence: A sustained, long-term downturn in the aerospace industry cycle could impair the normalized earnings power of the business.

valuation.downside_case: Transient cyclical earnings compression due to energy markets and destocking; long-term aerospace backlog secures baseline cash flows.

drivers.driver: The $37bn enterprise value purchase is an all-in bet on the structural growth of the aerospace industry, where the company maintains a dominant, sole-source position [D09].
Precision Castparts maintains a durable moat derived from technical certification and process expertise that acts as a significant barrier to entry [D01, D09].
Mark Donegan is an industry-leading operator whose retention ensures the business continues to be run with the owner-like discipline we require [D09].

The company's eight-year production backlog for major programs provides a level of earnings visibility that renders recent cyclical headwinds in energy and inventory management largely irrelevant to long-term value [D09].

kill_criteria: Aerospace manufacturing cycle experiences a long-term structural decline [D09].
Technical barriers to entry or sole-source status are eroded by new manufacturing technologies [D09].
Mark Donegan departs or ceases to operate with owner-like discipline [D09].
final.what_would_change_our_mind: A sustained, long-term downturn in the aerospace industry cycle that structurally impairs the business's normalized earnings power would invalidate our investment thesis.
final.memo:
Precision Castparts is a wonderful business that manufactures the critical, high-barrier metal components and fasteners essential to modern aerospace and industrial programs [D01, D09]. Charlie and I have long admired the company's ability to act as a sole or dominant supplier, a position earned through rigorous technical certification and process expertise that competitors find nearly impossible to replicate [D01, D09].

This is a company that has consistently demonstrated its economic strength, with operating margins historically exceeding 20% and returns on tangible capital regularly topping 20% [D09]. While the business is capital-intensive, it occupies such a dominant niche that it generates robust free cash flow, supported by a massive eight-year production backlog for major airframe and engine customers [D01, D09].

Mark Donegan, who has led the company since 2002, is an exceptional operator whom we trust implicitly [D09]. He will remain in place to run the business with the same owner-like discipline he has practiced for over a decade, allowing us to centralize capital allocation at Berkshire while leaving day-to-day operations under his proven guidance [D09].

Mr. Market is currently preoccupied with short-term cyclical headwinds, specifically in energy-related pipe markets and temporary destocking by aerospace customers [D09]. This noise has provided us the opportunity to acquire a high-quality enterprise at a fair price of $235 per share [D09]. When we look at a business with this durability, we do not focus on quarterly revenue fluctuations, but rather on the compounding power of the business over the next several decades [D09].

Our intrinsic value estimate comfortably brackets the $235 purchase price, and our expected return of 10% is far superior to the alternative of holding cash in a 2% yield environment [D04, D09]. We view this as a permanent addition to the Berkshire family, providing a productive home for a portion of our $66.6bn cash hoard [D09].

We recognize the risks of a long-term downturn in aerospace manufacturing or a change in the competitive landscape, but these are remote compared to the strength of the company's current backlog and technical position [D09]. This acquisition is an all-in wager on the economic future of the aerospace industry, a sector that will need Precision Castparts' specialized components for years to come [D09].
